title: Draw a sketch card
summary: Sketch an idea on its own sheet of paper, give it a name, and keep it beside your notes.
benefit: Try out a visual idea right next to the notes it belongs with.
outcome: A named sketch card sits on your board, and you can open it again to keep drawing.

sections.title: How sketches work
paragraphs: A sketch is a card with a sheet of paper in it. Draw on the paper with a pen, highlighter and eraser, give it a name, and the drawing stays inside the card when you move or resize it.
For example, draw the side view of a garden kennel next to your notes on what it needs. To mark up the board itself instead, use Draw.

flow.entry: In the tools on the left, choose Sketch under More, or drag it to the spot you want. On a phone, tap + at the bottom of the screen, then Sketch.

steps.action: Draw on the paper. Pick Pen or Highlighter, a colour and a line width in the bar at the top.
steps.result: Each stroke appears as you draw. Click, then Shift-click somewhere else, for a straight line.

steps.action: Click the title field (it says “Name this doodle”) and type a name, for example Kennel, side view.
steps.result: The name shows at the top of the sketch.

steps.action: Optionally, choose the paper icon at the far left to change the paper colour.
steps.result: The paper changes colour. The pen switches to white or charcoal if your ink would be hard to see on it.

steps.action: Choose Done, the tick at the top right, press Escape, or click outside the sketch.
steps.result: You're back on the board. The card shows your drawing with its name underneath.

flow.completion: Every stroke saves as soon as you finish it, and the sketch syncs to everyone on the board.
flow.correction: Use Undo and Redo, the curved arrows just before the pen, or ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z (Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z on Windows). The Eraser removes whole strokes, and one sweep is one Undo.

figures.alt: The sketch editor titled Kennel, side view. Across the top are the paper icon, the title, a zoom menu at 82% and a tick; below them Undo, Redo, pen, highlighter, eraser, ink colours and line widths. The paper shows a kennel outline with a red roof and a yellow highlighted ground line.

sections.title: Open a sketch again
paragraphs: Double-click the sketch card, or select it and press Enter, to reopen it with all its strokes ready to change. You can also right-click it and choose Edit. On a touch screen, tap the card once, then double-tap it.
To look closer, open the zoom menu at the top right of the sketch: Zoom in, Zoom out, Fit to window and Full screen.

sections.title: Arrange and copy sketches
paragraphs: Drag a sketch card wherever you like or drop it into a column. Drag its corner to resize it: the whole drawing scales with the card.

To try a variation, right-click the sketch and choose Duplicate, or press ⌘D (Ctrl+D on Windows). The copy has its own strokes, so changing it leaves the original alone. If you delete a sketch, find it in Buried bones, DoggyNote's bin in the tools on the left, and restore it with its drawing intact.

sections.title: Good to know
paragraphs: Mouse, trackpad, finger and stylus all draw. On a phone the sketch opens full screen.
People with view-only access see sketches on the board but can't change them. Sketches are included when you export the board with Export PNG.
